title: Private data-plane BGP flap during multi-region upgrade — instrumentation and mitigations
creator: Aisha Patel
summary: A rolling upgrade of the private orchestrator triggered a simultaneous BGP route flap across two regions. Control-plane agents lost stable data-plane reachability, causing job timeouts and a transient spike in reconnections. This ticket tracks instrumentation gaps discovered and concrete mitigations to prevent recurrence.
description:
What happened:
During the staged 2.9 private-controller rollout we deployed a control-plane change that unintentionally altered BGP advertisement timing on the orchestrator egress interfaces. Two downstream leaf routers in us-west-2 and eu-west-1 reacted by suppressing ECMP routes (route dampening heuristics), which led to asymmetric routing and intermittent control-plane agent connections to the data plane. Agent reconvergence cascaded into ephemeral port exhaustion on the orchestration side and token exchange failures for ~18 minutes in affected clusters.

Why it mattered:
- Control-plane requests (agent heartbeats, KV sync) saw elevated latencies and retries, surfacing as customer-facing API timeouts for private deployments on the affected regions.
- The orchestrator's retry logic amplified traffic (tight backoff) and contributed to ephemeral port exhaustion.
- Lack of per-region BGP instrumentation and missing canary-level route churn checks meant we didn't detect the pattern until alerts fired from downstream rate limits.

Scope and blast radius:
- 7 private clusters across 2 regions temporarily lost stable control-plane connectivity.
- Duration: ~18 minutes of elevated error rates, followed by ~40 minutes of increased reconnection noise during recovery.
timeline:
2026-03-11T03:12Z: Scheduled rolling upgrade begins
2026-03-11T03:25Z: First spike in agent reconnections detected (us-west-2)
2026-03-11T03:30Z: ECMP route oscillation observed by on-call network engineer
2026-03-11T03:34Z: Automated alert: orchestrator ephemeral port exhaustion threshold breached
2026-03-11T03:40Z: Rollout paused and partial rollback initiated
2026-03-11T03:50Z: Route dampening timers expired, ECMP restored; agents begin stable reconverge
2026-03-11T04:05Z: Rollout resumed with sequencing change and no further disruption
2026-03-11T05:10Z: Post-incident triage meeting scheduled
steps_taken: Paused the 2.9 rollout and rolled back the control-plane change in the two impacted regions (03:40-03:50Z).
Applied temporary increased ephemeral port allocation and extended orchestrator socket TIME_WAIT reuse to prevent immediate re-exhaustion.
Disabled the offending BGP advertisement timing tweak in the canary config and gated the change behind a feature flag.
Contacted network provider team to confirm no external flapping on physical links and validated route dampening thresholds on leaf routers.
Executed a focused observe-and-hold: resumed rollout with a single-cluster canary and extended monitoring windows for BGP churn metrics.
action_items: NET-1: Add per-region BGP churn metrics to the controller telemetry (net-agent + prometheus config) and create an alert for >3 route changes/min for critical prefixes — owner: Marco Rivera — due: 2026-03-18
ORCH-2: Implement graceful orchestrator backoff that caps concurrent reconnect attempts per-cluster to avoid port exhaustion — owner: Priya Sharma — due: 2026-03-21
DEPLOY-3: Update rolling upgrade sequencer to enforce inter-region gaps and require canary success threshold before cross-region expansion — owner: Liam O'Connor — due: 2026-03-20
TEST-4: Add a synthetic canary that induces controlled BGP advertisement timing variance in staging to validate dampening behavior before prod rollout — owner: Jaime Nguyen — due: 2026-03-25
DOC-5: Update private deployment runbook with BGP troubleshooting checklist and explicit rollback playbook including port exhaustion remediation steps — owner: Aisha Patel — due: 2026-03-17
notes: Root cause is a timing/interplay issue between a control-plane egress adjustment and conservative route-dampening on leaf routers. We observed that our orchestrator lacks any soft-circuit breaker for reconnect storm protection. Prioritized fixes split into short-term observability + operational controls and medium-term sequencer and backoff logic. Coordination with Network Infra team required for permanent dampening tuning.
